correctness.rationale: For every \(i\), exact one-point and two-point permutation conditioning yields \((n-f)/[n(n-1)]\) when \(\eta(i)=i\) and \(2f/[n(n-1)(n-2)]\) otherwise; summation proves the identity for all \(n\ge3\). The proof checks feasibility of \(f\), the sharp quadratic maximum, zero-covariance yet dependent boundary, and the density limit. A standalone reproducible enumeration verifies 876 exact reference-permutation cases comprising 669492 ordered permutation pairs. Finite checks are not used as the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The strongest directly relevant primary literature establishes the commutator-count definition, marginal mean/Poisson law, general marginal character moments, and unweighted k-commuting counts. They do not state or mathematically imply the same-permutation cross covariance from their published marginal statements. Exact structural dependence solely on f and the sharp uncorrelated-but-dependent derangement boundary were compared against literature aliases and published records. Unknown older joint formulas remain a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: A historical character-theoretic joint-moment formula for permutation characters and commutators may implicitly entail this exact identity without using these keywords.
Published published-finding corpus search is limited to indexed public records; unpublished work and unindexed papers are not excluded.
The covariance identity does not imply probabilistic independence even when zero; no joint distribution theorem is claimed.

value.rationale: The covariance addresses a natural joint dependence gap for two fixed-point statistics on the same uniformly shuffled permutation; it is not an arbitrary narrow numerical slice. The complete finite cycle-type classification shows a sharp universal nonnegative sign, exact vanishing for every derangement despite dependence, positive covariance for partial fixed support, and a sharp extremal value with nontrivial density limit. Marginal results depending on two-cycles do not predict this cycle-structure blindness; the result is a motivated structural statistic of near-commutation.
